articleTitle: The Kato–Nakayama Space as a Transcendental Root Stack
abstract: We give a functorial description of the Kato–Nakayama space of a fine saturated log analytic space, that is similar in spirit to the functorial description of root stacks. As a consequence we get a global description of the comparison map constructed in [2] from the Kato–Nakayama space to the (topological) infinite root stack.

articleTitle: Graded Leinster Monoids and Generalized Deligne Conjecture for 1-Monoidal Abelian Categories
abstract: In our recent paper Shoikhet [47], a version of the “generalized Deligne conjecture” for abelian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-fold monoidal categories is proven. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=1,$</tex> this result says that, given an abelian monoidal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Bbbk$</tex>-linear category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex> with unit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\operatorname{char}}\Bbbk=0$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm{RHom}}_{\mathcal{A}}(e,e)$</tex> is the first component of a Leinster 1-monoid in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{A}lg}}(\Bbbk)$</tex> (provided a rather mild condition on the monoidal and the abelian structures in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>, called homotopy compatibility, is fulfilled). In this article, we introduce a new concept of a graded Leinster monoid. We show that the Leinster monoid in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{A}lg}}(\Bbbk)$</tex>, constructed by a monoidal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Bbbk$</tex>-linear abelian category in Shoikhet [47], is graded. We construct a functor, assigning an algebra over the chain operad <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{{{{\bullet}}}}(E_2,\Bbbk)$</tex>, to a graded Leinster 1-monoid in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{A}lg}}(\Bbbk)$</tex>, which respects the weak equivalences. Consequently, this article together with Shoikhet [47] provides a complete proof of the “generalized Deligne conjecture” for 1-monoidal abelian categories, in the form most accessible for applications to deformation theory (such as Tamarkin’s proof of the Kontsevich formality).

We prove in this article that the set of semi-hyperbolic rational maps has Lebesgue measure zero in the space of rational maps on the Riemann sphere for a fixed degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d \geq 2$</tex>. This extends the earlier result [3] to its full generality.

articleTitle: Nonparametric Mean Curvature Type Flows of Graphs with Contact Angle Conditions
abstract: In this article, we study nonparametric mean curvature type flows in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M{\mkern-1mu\times\mkern-1mu}\mathbb{R}$</tex> which are represented as graphs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(x,u(x,t))$</tex> over a domain in a Riemannian manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> with prescribed contact angle. The speed of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex> is the mean curvature speed minus an admissible function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi(x,u,Du)$</tex>. Long time existence and uniformly convergence are established if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi(x,u, Du)\equiv 0$</tex> with vertical contact angle and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi(x,u,Du)=h(x,u)\sqrt{1+|Du|^2}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h_u(x,u)\geq h_0>0$</tex>. Their applications include mean curvature type equations with prescribed contact angle boundary condition and the asymptotic behavior of nonparametric mean curvature flows of graphs over a convex domain in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M^2$</tex> which is a surface with nonnegative Ricci curvature.

Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> be a field complete with respect to a discrete valuation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v$</tex> of residue characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(z) \in K[z]$</tex> be a separable polynomial of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z^\ell-c$</tex>. Given <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a \in K$</tex>, we examine the Galois groups and ramification groups of the extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> generated by the solutions to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f^n(z)=a$</tex>. The behavior depends upon <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v(c)$</tex>, and we find that it shifts dramatically as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v(c)$</tex> crosses a certain value: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex> in the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \nmid \ell$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-p/(p-1)$</tex> in the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=\ell$</tex>.

articleTitle: Ehrhart Theory of Spanning Lattice Polytopes
abstract: The key object in the Ehrhart theory of lattice polytopes is the numerator polynomial of the rational generating series of the Ehrhart polynomial, called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^*$</tex>-polynomial. In this article, we prove a new result on the vanishing of its coefficients. As a consequence, we get that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^*_i =0$</tex> implies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^*_{i+1}=0$</tex> if the lattice points of the lattice polytope affinely span the ambient lattice. This generalizes a recent result in algebraic geometry due to Blekherman, Smith, and Velasco, and implies a polyhedral consequence of the Eisenbud–Goto conjecture. We also discuss how this study is motivated by unimodality questions and how it relates to decomposition results on lattice polytopes of given degree. The proof methods involve a novel combination of successive modifications of half-open triangulations and considerations of number-theoretic step functions.

articleTitle: Multispeed Klein–Gordon Systems in Dimension Three
abstract: We consider long-time evolution of small solutions to general multispeed Klein–Gordon systems on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{3}$</tex>. We prove that such solutions are always global and scatter to a linear flow, thus extending partial results obtained previously in Germain [5], Germain and Masmoudi [15] and Ionescu and Pausader [4]. The main new ingredient of our method is an improved linear dispersion estimate exploiting the spherical symmetry of the Klein–Gordon flow, and a corresponding bilinear oscillatory integral estimate.

Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> be a smooth curve embedded in a smooth quasi-projective three-fold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q^n_C={\text{Quot}}_n(\mathscr I_C)$</tex> be the Quot scheme of length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> quotients of its ideal sheaf. We show the identity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde\chi(Q^n_C)=(-1)^n\chi(Q^n_C)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde\chi$</tex> is the Behrend weighted Euler characteristic. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> is a projective Calabi–Yau three-fold, this shows that the Donaldson–Thomas (DT) contribution of a smooth rigid curve is the signed Euler characteristic of the moduli space. This can be rephrased as a DT/PT wall-crossing type formula, which can be formulated for arbitrary smooth curves. In general, such wall-crossing formula is shown to be equivalent to a certain Behrend function identity.
